gloss: hate; set against, set aside; hater, enemy
summary: To hate: to set oneself against a person or thing, the opposite of אָהֵב “love” in nearly every context (Psa 45:8; Amo 5:15; Ecc 3:8). It runs from settled ill will that can end in murder (Gen 37:4; Deu 19:11), through turning against a wife and putting her away (Deu 22:13; 24:3), to the “hate” of comparison, where the one hated is the one loved less or not chosen (Gen 29:30–31; Deu 21:15; Mal 1:2–3). Yahweh hates evil and empty worship (Pro 6:16; Isa 61:8; Amo 5:21), and those who fear him hate evil too (Pro 8:13); the participle שֹׂנֵא, with the piel מְשַׂנֵּא, is “the one who hates”, the enemy, constantly beside אֹיֵב (Num 10:35). Arabic شَنِئَ “hate”, Ugaritic šnʾ, Phoenician šnʾt “hatred” and Sabaic šnʾ “enemy” share the meaning.

words.summary: About 145 uses. The qal’s active participle שֹׂנֵא is often a noun, “one who hates, enemy”, and its passive participle שְׂנוּאָה “the hated (wife)”; the piel is found only as the participle מְשַׂנֵּא, in the same sense as שֹׂנֵא, and the niphal twice, “be hated”.

stems.gloss: hate; reject; love less; (participle) hater, enemy

senses.definition: To be set against another person in the heart, so that one cannot speak peaceably with him and wishes or plans him harm; the law’s mark of the deliberate killer, who “hated him beforehand” and lay in wait for him.

evidence.note: Joseph’s brothers “hated him, and could not speak peaceably to him”.
“They hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words.”
“You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your neighbour”: hatred is kept inside, set against open rebuke and, in the next verse, love of the neighbour.
“If a man hates his neighbour, and lies in wait for him, and rises up against him, and strikes him”: hatred acted on.
The manslayer “did not hate him beforehand”.
Isaac to Abimelech: “you hate me, and have sent me away from you”.
Jephthah: “did you not hate me, and drive me out of my father’s house?”
Absalom hated Amnon, and spoke to him neither good nor bad, until he killed him.
“All the brothers of the poor man hate him.”
A neighbour who has had too much of you will hate you.
Ahab hates Micaiah, “for he does not prophesy good about me, but evil”.
Yahweh turned Egypt’s heart “to hate his people, to deal craftily with his servants”.
“Your brothers who hated you, who cast you out for my name’s sake.”
Given into the hand of “those whom you hate, from whom your soul is alienated”.

senses.definition: The active participle שֹׂנֵא as a noun: the one who hates someone, his enemy, set beside אֹיֵב as its equal; in war, in the covenant’s curses and blessings, and in personal strife.

evidence.note: “He delivered me from my strong enemy (אֹיְבִי), and from those who hated me (וּמִשֹּׂנְאַי).”
“You shall be struck down before your enemies; those who hate you shall rule over you.”
“He saved them from the hand of the one who hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.” Echoed in Luk 1:71.
“The donkey of one who hates you”, after “your enemy’s ox” in 23:4: help it all the same.
“If the one who hates you is hungry, give him bread to eat”; quoted in Rom 12:20 as ἐχθρός.
“May your seed possess the gate of those who hate them.”
“On your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you.”
“Those who hated them ruled over them.”
“Those who hate me without cause.”
“Deceitful are the kisses of one who hates.”
The Jews ruled over those who hated them.
Joab to David: “you love those who hate you, and hate those who love you”.

senses.definition: Where two are set side by side, the one “hated” is the one loved less, passed over for the other: no ill will need be meant, only that the other is preferred or chosen.

evidence.note: Jacob “loved Rachel more than Leah”, and Yahweh “saw that Leah was hated (שְׂנוּאָה)”.
Leah names Simeon: “Yahweh heard that I am hated.”
Two wives, “the one loved and the other hated”: the hated one’s son keeps the firstborn’s double portion.
“I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated”: the choice of one brother’s line over the other’s; quoted in Rom 9:13 of election before birth.
“He who spares his rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him”: not doing what love would do.
“A hated woman when she is married.”
Zion, “forsaken and hated”, made an eternal pride.
Samson’s wife: “you only hate me, and do not love me”, because he kept the riddle from her.

senses.definition: Of a husband toward his wife: to turn against her and send her away; in the law’s cases the word that leads to the bill of divorce.

evidence.note: “If the latter husband hates her, and writes her a bill of divorce, and puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house.”
“If a man takes a wife, and goes in to her, and hates her”, and then brings false charges to be rid of her.
Samson’s father-in-law: “I surely thought you utterly hated her, so I gave her to your companion.”
“For he hates sending away (שַׁלַּח), says Yahweh, the God of Israel”: the putting away of the wife of one’s youth (2:14–15).
Amnon hated Tamar more than he had loved her, and said, “Get up, go.”

senses.definition: To abhor a deed or way and refuse it: what Yahweh hates is what is abomination to him, and those who love and fear him hate evil, falsehood and unjust gain in the same way.

evidence.note: “These six things Yahweh hates, and seven are an abomination (תּוֹעֲבַת) to him.”
“Every abomination to Yahweh, which he hates, they have done to their gods.”
“I Yahweh love justice; I hate robbery with burnt offering.”
A pillar, “which Yahweh your God hates”.
“Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hates.”
“I hate, I despise your feasts.”
Evil plotted against a neighbour and a false oath: “all these are things that I hate”.
“Do not do this abominable thing that I hate.”
“You hate all workers of iniquity.”
“The one who loves violence his soul hates.”
“There I hated them … I will love them no more.”
“The fear of Yahweh is to hate evil.”
“Hate evil, and love good, and establish justice in the gate.”
“You who love Yahweh, hate evil.”
The king “loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God … anointed you”; quoted of the Son in Heb 1:9.
“I hate every false way.”
“I hate and abhor falsehood; your law I love.”
“I hate the work of those who turn aside.”
“I have hated the assembly of evildoers.”
“Do I not hate those who hate you, Yahweh? … I hate them with complete hatred.”
Judges are to be “men of truth, hating unjust gain”.
“He who hates bribes will live.”

senses.gloss: hate (what is good: God, his correction)
senses.definition: The hatred of the wicked and the fool for what is good: for knowledge, instruction and rebuke, for the one who speaks uprightly, and for God himself, shown in not keeping his commandments.

evidence.note: “Of those who hate me”, set against “those who love me and keep my commandments”.
“He repays those who hate him to their face, to destroy them.”
“Because they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of Yahweh.”
“You hate instruction, and cast my words behind you.”
“Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is stupid.”
“How I hated instruction!”
“Do not reprove a scoffer, lest he hate you.”
“They hate him who reproves in the gate, and abhor him who speaks uprightly.”
Israel’s rulers, “who hate good and love evil”.
“Shall one who hates justice govern?”
“With him who hates peace.”
“Should you help the wicked and love those who hate Yahweh?”

senses.definition: To turn in disgust from one’s own life or labour, finding nothing in it worth keeping.

evidence.note: “So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me.”
“I hated all my labour”, since it must be left to another.
“Whoever is partner with a thief hates his own soul.”
“A time to love, and a time to hate.”

senses.gloss: one who hates, enemy (of Yahweh, his king, his people)
senses.definition: Found only as the participle מְשַׂנֵּא, used as the qal participle is, for the enemy, nearly always beside אֹיֵב; most often of those who hate Yahweh or the king he upholds, and once of those who hate wisdom. The text does not show that it is stronger than שֹׂנֵא: the same psalm uses both (Psa 18:18, 41).

evidence.note: When the ark set out: “Rise up, Yahweh, and let your enemies (אֹיְבֶיךָ) be scattered, and let those who hate you (מְשַׂנְאֶיךָ) flee before you.”
The words of Num 10:35 taken up: “Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee before him.”
“I will render vengeance to my adversaries, and repay those who hate me.”
“Strike the loins of those who rise against him, and of those who hate him.”
“You gave me the necks of my enemies, those who hated me, and I destroyed them”; also 2Sa 22:41.
“Those who hate Yahweh would cringe before him.”
“Your enemies make a tumult, and those who hate you have lifted up their head.”
“I will beat down his adversaries before him, and strike those who hate him”, of David’s seed.
“Do I not hate those who hate you (מְשַׂנְאֶיךָ), Yahweh?”
“You have saved us from our adversaries, and put to shame those who hate us.”
“It was not one who hated me who exalted himself against me”, but a companion.
Job did not rejoice at the ruin of one who hated him.
Wisdom: “all who hate me love death.”

senses.definition: To be the object of others’ hatred: the schemer for his schemes, the poor man for his poverty.

evidence.note: “The poor is hated even by his neighbour, but the rich has many friends (אֹהֲבֵי).”
“A man of wicked schemes is hated.”

evidence.locator: Mal.1.3, שָׂנֵאתִי → ἐμίσησα; Psa.45.8, תִּשְׂנָא → ἐμίσησας; Lev.19.17, תִשְׂנָא → μισήσεις; Psa.106.10, שׂוֹנֵא → μισούντων; Gen.29.31, שְׂנוּאָה → μισεῖται; Psa.68.2, מְשַׂנְאָיו → μισοῦντες; μισέω renders שָׂנֵא ×98 (MACULA alignment)

evidence.note: Mal 1:2–3 quoted: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated (ἐμίσησα)”, of God’s choice made before the twins were born (9:11–12).
Psa 45:8 quoted of the Son: “You loved righteousness and hated (ἐμίσησας) lawlessness.”
“That the word written in their law might be fulfilled, ‘They hated (ἐμίσησαν) me without a cause’” (Psa 35:19; 69:5).
“If the world hates you, you know that it hated me before it hated you.”
“Salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate (μισούντων) us”, the words of Psa 106:10 and 18:18.
“You shall love your neighbour (Lev 19:18) and hate your enemy … but I say, love your enemies, do good to those who hate you.”
“Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer”: Lev 19:17 read with the law of the manslayer.
“If anyone … does not hate his father and mother”, which Mat 10:37 gives as “loves father or mother more than me”.

evidence.locator: Pro.25.21, שֹׂנַאֲךָ → ἐχθρός; ἐχθρός renders שָׂנֵא ×10 (MACULA alignment)

evidence.note: Pro 25:21–22 quoted: “If your enemy (ἐχθρός) is hungry, feed him.”

parallels.note: “Enemy”: the participle’s constant pair, in either order.

evidence.note: מִתְקוֹמְמֶיךָ, “those who rise up against you”.

parallels.note: “Abomination”: what Yahweh hates is what is abominable to him.

opposites.note: “Love”: the opposite in almost every passage where the two meet.

phrases.gloss: those who hate me without cause

evidence.note: Fulfilled in the hatred of Jesus.

of those who hate me (in the Ten Words)

words.summary: The verbal noun: hatred, the opposite of אַהֲבָה “love”.

senses.definition: Hatred held against another, the opposite of love; in the law, the hatred that makes a killing murder.

evidence.note: “Amnon hated her with very great hatred, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her.”
“If he pushed him in hatred … or struck him in enmity (בְאֵיבָה)”, he is a murderer; “if suddenly, without enmity”, not.
“Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all transgressions.”
“Hatred in return for my love.”
“Words of hatred … without cause.”
“Better a dinner of herbs where love is than a fattened ox and hatred with it.”
“He who hides hatred has lying lips.”
Hatred covered by deceit is uncovered before the assembly.
“They hate me with violent hatred.”
Edom’s “hatreds” against Israel, which Yahweh will repay.
“They shall deal with you in hatred.”
“Whether love or hatred, man does not know.”
The dead: “their love, their hatred and their envy have now perished.”

senses.definition: The hatred the righteous bear toward those who set themselves against Yahweh, complete and undivided.

evidence.note: “I hate them with complete hatred (תַּכְלִית שִׂנְאָה); they have become my enemies.”

senses.definition: The hatred unbelief imputes to Yahweh in his dealings: Israel’s murmuring, and the nations’ taunt Moses feared.

evidence.note: “Because Yahweh hated us, he brought us out of the land of Egypt, to give us into the hand of the Amorites.”
Lest the nations say Yahweh brought Israel out “because he hated them”.

evidence.locator: Num.35.20, בְּשִׂנְאָה → ἔχθραν; ἔχθρα renders שִׂנְאָה ×3, μῖσος (not in the New Testament) ×8 (MACULA alignment)

evidence.note: “The mind of the flesh is enmity (ἔχθρα) against God, for it is not subject to the law of God.”
“Friendship with the world is enmity with God.”

parallels.note: “Enmity”, in the law of the manslayer.

words.summary: Once, in the law of the two wives, beside the passive participle שְׂנוּאָה in the same sense; a form like a passive participle, with nothing in the verse to tell it apart from שְׂנוּאָה.

senses.definition: The wife loved less than the other, whose son is nonetheless the firstborn.

evidence.note: “If the firstborn son is hers that is hated (לַשְּׂנִיאָה)”, after “one loved and the other hated (שְׂנוּאָה)”.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, once, as the participle “those who hate you”, beside עָר “adversary”.

senses.definition: Daniel wishes the dream on the king’s haters and its interpretation on his adversaries: the participle as noun, as Hebrew שֹׂנֵא.

evidence.note: “My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you (לְשָׂנְאָךְ, read שָׂנְאָיִךְ), and its interpretation for your adversaries (לְעָרָךְ).”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܣܢܐ (snā), where the Greek has μισέω: the Aramaic form of the root, with s for ś.

senses.definition: To hate, as the Hebrew: the world’s hatred of Jesus and his disciples, God’s “hating” Esau, the Son’s hatred of lawlessness, and the disciple’s “hating” father and mother, that is loving them less than Christ.

evidence.note: “They hated me without a cause”, Psa 35:19 and 69:5 fulfilled.
Mal 1:3: “Esau I hated.”
Psa 45:8 of the Son.
Hating father and mother: Mat 10:37 has “loves … more than me”.
“Whoever hates his brother is a murderer.”
“He who hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܣܢܐܐ (sānʾā), the agent noun, for Greek οἱ μισοῦντες, as Hebrew שֹׂנֵא.

senses.definition: Those who hate someone, set beside his enemies.

evidence.note: “From our enemies, and from the hand of all who hate us”: Psa 106:10 and 18:18.
“Love your enemies … do good to those who hate you.”

senses.definition: Hated by others; of the disciples, hated by all for Christ’s name.

evidence.note: “You will be hated by all for my name’s sake.”

cognates.note: Arabic š answers to Hebrew ś. The verb, its active participle “hater, enemy”, the noun “(vehement) hatred” and the passive “hated” match the Hebrew verb, participle שֹׂנֵא, noun שִׂנְאָה and passive שָׂנוּא / שָׂנִיא one for one.

evidence.note: “He hated him … or, as some say, he hated him vehemently.”
“Hating, or a hater, … and an enemy.”
“Hatred … vehement hatred.”
“Hated, or rendered hateful, or an object of hatred.”

cognates.note: In the Karatepe inscription, “out of love or out of hatred”, the same pair as Hebrew אַהֲבָה and שִׂנְאָה (2Sa 13:15; Pro 10:12).

evidence.note: “[Heb. sinʾa] n.f. HATRED. KAI 26 A III 17/18 (Ph) … ‘Whether he shall pull it [the gate] up out of love or out of hatred or pull the gate up out of malice.’”

evidence.locator: SEM001060 śnʾt [hate] N, PUN002007 šnʾt [hatred] N

cognates.note: Old South Arabian (Sabaean) noun “enemy”, very common in prayers to be kept from “(any) enemy, far or near”: the sense of the Hebrew participle שֹׂנֵא. Sabaean s² answers to Hebrew ś.

evidence.note: “n s S²nʾ(m,n) … ENEMY [Cf Heb śōnēʾ id, Ar šanaʾa ‘hate.’]”; R3991/16, “from harm, injurer(s), injury or evil eye of (any) enemy”.

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud, written with ס or שׂ: the verb renders Hebrew שָׂנֵא (Targ. Onkelos Deu 22:13, 16), the noun שִׂנְאָה (Num 35:20), and the agent noun שֹׂנֵא (Exo 23:5; Psa 35:19).

evidence.note: “to hate. Targ. O. Deut. XXII, 16 … Ib. 13. Targ. Ps. XXXI, 7 … (interch. with שְׂ׳).”
“hatred. Targ. Y. Ex. XXIII, 5. Targ. Y. Num. XXXV, 20.”
“hater, enemy. Targ. Ex. XXIII, 5”; plural at Targ. Ps. XXXV, 19.

doctrine.statement: Jacob “loved Rachel more than Leah”, and the next verse says Leah “was hated” (Gen 29:30–31): the hatred is the lesser love. The law speaks of two wives, “one loved and the other hated”, and still gives the hated wife’s son the firstborn’s right (Deu 21:15–17). Yahweh says “I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated” (Mal 1:2–3), and Paul quotes it of the choice made “before the children were born or had done anything good or bad, that God’s purpose according to election might stand” (Rom 9:11–13). Jesus says that whoever “does not hate his father and mother … cannot be my disciple” (Luk 14:26), which Matthew records as “whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me” (Mat 10:37). From the verses: where scripture sets two side by side, to “hate” the one is to put the other first; God’s hatred of Esau is his choice of Jacob’s line for the promise, and the disciple’s hatred of his family is loving them less than Christ, not ill will toward them.

The law says “you shall not hate your brother in your heart”, but rebuke him openly and love him as yourself (Lev 19:17–18). It parts the murderer from the manslayer by this word: the one who “hated his neighbour, and lay in wait for him” is put to death (Deu 19:11–12; Num 35:20–21), while the one who “did not hate him beforehand” may flee to a city of refuge (Deu 19:4–6; Jos 20:5). John draws the conclusion: “everyone who hates his brother is a murderer” (1Jn 3:15), and he who hates his brother walks in darkness (1Jn 2:9–11). The same law bids help for the donkey “of one who hates you” (Exo 23:5), and Proverbs bids bread for the hungry hater (Pro 25:21), which Paul quotes (Rom 12:20); Jesus says, “love your enemies, do good to those who hate you” (Mat 5:44; Luk 6:27). From the verses: hatred kept in the heart is already what the law punishes when it is acted out, and the answer to the one who hates is to do him good.

Scripture names what Yahweh hates: the six things that are an abomination to him (Pro 6:16–19), robbery dressed as offering (Isa 61:8), feasts kept by hands full of blood (Isa 1:14–15; Amo 5:21–24), evil plotted against a neighbour and false oaths (Zec 8:17), and the one who loves violence (Psa 11:5). “The fear of Yahweh is to hate evil” (Pro 8:13), and those who love him are told “hate evil” (Psa 97:10; Amo 5:15). Of the king it is said, “you loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, your God, anointed you” (Psa 45:8), and Hebrews reads it of the Son (Heb 1:9). From the verses: to love Yahweh is to hate what he hates, and the anointed king was so in full; worship that does not hate evil is itself what Yahweh hates.

David speaks of “those who hate me without cause” (Psa 35:19; 69:5), who return “hatred for my love” (Psa 109:3–5). Jesus says the world’s hatred of him fulfils “the word written in their law, ‘They hated me without a cause’” (Jhn 15:25), and that the world which hated him first will hate his disciples (Jhn 15:18–19); “you will be hated by all for my name’s sake” (Mat 10:22), as Isaiah spoke of brothers “who hated you, who cast you out for my name’s sake” (Isa 66:5). From the verses: the hatred David suffered from his own people was the pattern of the hatred of the Son of David, and his followers share it for his name.

In the Ten Words, Yahweh visits iniquity “of those who hate me” and shows mercy “to those who love me and keep my commandments” (Exo 20:5–6; Deu 5:9–10); he “repays those who hate him to their face” (Deu 7:10). Wisdom says “all who hate me love death” (Pro 8:36), and the simple are those who “hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of Yahweh” (Pro 1:29). Jesus says “if you love me, keep my commandments” (Jhn 14:15), and “he who hates me hates my Father also” (Jhn 15:23). From the verses: hating God is not a feeling scripture looks for but a way of life, refusing his commandments and his correction, and its end is death.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Numbers 10 (מְשַׂנְאֶיךָ, Num 10:35). Root key שׂנא as the corpus keys it. Biblical Aramaic שְׂנָא (xu.af.aa) has 0 counted tokens: its one use, Dan 4:16 ketiv לְשָׂנְאָךְ (qere שָׂנְאָיִךְ), is not keyed to any lexicon entry in the database, so lexicon-support will show it with no uses. The brief files Pro 28:16 שֹׂנֵא (qere; ketiv שׂנאי) under root נוא; it is this verb (“he who hates unjust gain”) and should count here. Left out: the place name שְׂנִיר Senir (u.bq.ad, 4 uses: Deu 3:9; 1Ch 5:23; Sng 4:8; Ezk 27:5), the Amorite name of Hermon (Deu 3:9), which is a place and cannot be a name entry, and whose link to “hate” is not shown. The brief’s Peshitta section lists ܫܢܐ (tooth; be mad), a different root; the Peshitta’s “hate” is ܣܢܐ, SEDRA root 1292 SNA, lexemes 2162 SNA (verb, hate), 2163 SN;A (hateful), 2164 SNAA (hater), 2165 SN;AA (hated); verse lists found from BFBS.TXT. SN;A “hateful” (Jhn 3:20, Eph 4:29, Rev 18:2 in the SEDRA list) not entered; SNA verb also listed at Act 28:5–6, Tit 1:14 and Tit 2:8 in SEDRA, not read. Krahmalkov p. 473 and Biella p. 519 read from the text layers only (OCR: Krahmalkov’s headword shows as “SNT”, Biella’s as “Snr”), page images unverified; the forms follow the quoted inscriptions and Anderson–Moser’s šnʾt. Ugaritic šnʾ cited from Anderson–Moser only (not in Segert’s glossary; DULAT not consulted); the aleph sign 𐎀 is conventional. Not consulted: Geʿez (Dillmann, Leslau); CAL and DEAPS for Imperial Aramaic, where the Elephantine marriage contracts use śnʾ for a spouse’s declaring divorce, which would bear on the sense “put away a wife” and Mal 2:16. No Akkadian cognate found (Oracc’s šn- candidates mean “second, change, tooth”). Open questions: (1) the reading of Mal 2:16 כִּי־שָׂנֵא שַׁלַּח (subject Yahweh, “he hates sending away”); (2) whether the piel participle is more than a variant of the qal participle.
